source.title: Belfast Newsletter, 8 June 1964, p. 9 ("Hillsborough Rural District Council: notice of result of elections, 1964"); Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1964, p. 2 ("Hillsborough Labour man polls 17 votes")

source.check: names and votes read on the page images: the returning officer's notice of result (8 June 1964, p. 9), where Crossey's row sits on the Maze line, and the results paragraph of 5 June 1964, p. 2, which gives Maze as Fullerton 307, Crossey (Lab.) 204 (council-audit, Nov 2026).

note: Triennial election of Hillsborough Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Hillsborough, Maze and Anahilt were contested and the other thirteen divisions were returned unopposed. Maze: David Campbell Fullerton 307, William Thompson Crossey (Lab.) 204; 80.73 per cent poll (Belfast News-Letter, 5 June 1964, p. 2). Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026).
correctionNote: Corrected from the page images of the Belfast News-Letter, 8 June 1964, p. 9 and 5 June 1964, p. 2 (council-audit, Nov 2026): William Thompson Crossey (Lab.), 204 votes, was the defeated candidate in Maze (his row sits on the Maze line of the notice and the 5 June report lists him under Maze); he had been filed under Hillsborough division and is moved here; the note no longer says Maze had a single candidate.
